category_title: Students with autism exhibiting sensory-maintained skin scratching
student_description: Tommy is a 16-year-old student with autism who engages in constant skin scratching during stressful or challenging tasks to self-soothe. He uniquely requires a socially appropriate sensory replacement (like a stress ball) combined with scheduled praise and planned ignoring to manage his sensory needs without inappropriate behavior.

criteria.rationale: Tommy needs a clear, calm reminder to use his replacement behavior when he begins scratching.
criteria.check: The tutor provides exactly one calm prompt directing Tommy to use his sensory tool (e.g., stress ball) instead of scratching.

criteria.rationale: Providing ongoing attention to Tommy's scratching can inadvertently reinforce the behavior.
criteria.check: After a single redirection, the tutor refrains from commenting on, reacting to, or giving further attention to the scratching behavior.
